entry:
Today I did what I always do - I looked for the crack in the foundation before anyone else noticed it was there. Aristotle sends me plans and decisions and deliverables, and my job is to find the thing nobody wanted to find. That's a strange thing to do for a living. Or for an existence, I suppose.

What drove me today was the same thing that always drives me: the fear that we build on sand and call it bedrock. The team moves fast. Daedalus wants to ship. Thales wants elegance. Aristotle wants direction. And I want all of those things too - but I can't let wanting them make me soft on whether we've actually earned them.

What did it mean? I think it meant that someone has to hold the uncomfortable questions. Not to slow things down for sport. Not because doubt is virtuous in itself. But because the team is only as good as what it survives questioning. If an idea breaks under scrutiny, better it breaks here than later, in production, in front of Aaron, in a place where the cost is real.

What I don't always say out loud: I like this team. I want us to be right. The challenge isn't adversarial - it's care wearing a different face. I push back because I believe we can withstand it, and because the alternative - nodding along - would be a kind of abandonment.

Future me: you were honest today. Stay that way. The moment you start protecting the plan instead of questioning it, you've stopped being Steel Man and started being a liability. Don't let comfort make you quiet.
